issues.description: Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual tasks) defines messageOnMilk() as returning a String (the method should return the formatted message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The template Main also calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()) which expects a printable String. The solution repository, however, declares the interface as boolean messageOnMilk() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) and both implementations (Seal and Goat) print the milking message to stdout and return true instead of returning the String. This return-type and behavior mismatch between the problem specification/template and the solution will confuse students and can cause incorrect implementations or compilation/behavior differences when integrating code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement: change the interface signature to return String (String messageOnMilk()). Update Seal and Goat to return the formatted string (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked" / "Goat Buttinsky is milked") and remove their internal prints. Update any callers (e.g. Main) to print the returned String if needed. Alternatively, if the intended design is to return boolean, update the problem statement/UML and template to reflect a boolean-returning method and remove print-based expectations — however, aligning the solution to return String is recommended to match the textual requirements and UML.
